title: 超千户失信主体补税金约13.6亿元完成信用修复
content_preview: 1219户失信主体补税金后申请提前停止公布失信信息 中国为了惩罚重大税收违法行为，税务部门会对外公开曝光重大税收违法失信主体的相关信息，失信企业的经营将受到影响。不过在企业税法遵从意识提升和信用修复更加便捷等因素推动下，越来越多的失信主体积极补税加快信用修复。 10月12日，税务总局公开数据显示，今年前9个月，税务部门共停止公布失信主体12028户，其中，除依规到期自动停止公布外，1219户失信主体通过缴清税款、滞纳金、罚款共计13.55亿元后，申请提前停止公布，实现信用修复，修复总量同比增长30.93%，这表明依法诚信纳税越来越成为经营主体的共识。 中央财经大学财政税务学院院长樊勇表示，对于失信主体必须进行惩戒，让其在市场经济中处处受限，这是法治社会公平正义的体现，也是建设市场经济的必要举措。但惩戒只是手段，引导企业依法诚信经营才是目的。税务机关在实施失信惩戒的同时开展信用修复，有利于提升纳税人的税法遵从意识。 根据税务总局2021年修订发布《重大税收违法失信主体信息公布管理办法》（下称《办法》），重大税收违法失信主体主要有11种情形，比如偷逃税、欠税超100万元的；骗取国家出口退税款；虚开增值税普通发票100份以上或者金额400万元以上等。 经过相应程序后，上述失信主体的基本情况、主要税收违法事实、处罚等信息都会被税务部门公开对外披露。 上述税收违法案件信息对外公布后，失信主体的纳税信用等级直接降为D级，在贷款融资、资质许可、项目投标、商业合作等方面都会受到较大制约。 不过上述《办法》新增信用修复相关内容。比如明确失信主体按照《税务处理决定书》《税务行政处罚决定书》缴清（退）税款、滞纳金、罚款，且失信主体失信信息公布满六个月的，可以向作出确定失信主体决定的税务机关申请提前停止公布失信信息。信用修复后，企业可重新评定纳税信用等级，融资、招投标等经营活动不再受限，重新恢复正常经营。 税务总局稽查局有关负责人介绍，为使纳税失信约束惩戒和信用修复制度充分发挥治理效能，保障失信主体依法申请信用修复的权利，税务部门积极实践、探索行之有效的工作方法，以机制创新推动信用修复更加便捷高效。 比如，为便利失信主体快速修复，税务部门协调发展和改革委相关部门在“信用中国”网站增设信用修复模块，该模块开通后，失信主体除可向税务机关当面提交信用修复申请外，还可通过“信用中国”网站进行线上申请和提交资料，形成线上线下协同办理模式。2026年以来，已有511户失信主体通过“信用中国”网站完成线上信用修复，占今年信用修复总量的42%。 另外，税务部门还通过“说理式”执法等手段，向失信主体深入解读政策和失信后果等，引导失信主体积极主动进行信用修复。 上述负责人表示，下一步，税务部门在强化重大税收违法失信主体管理的同时，将持续优化信用修复流程，加强信用修复政策宣传辅导，努力实现“到期即提醒、达标即修复”，助力更多企业重塑信用、合规经营。

title: 【多地证监局发文 明确930金融网络营销新规具体要求】监管正强调与督促券商、基金公司落地实施“930新规”。《金融产品网
content_preview: 【多地证监局发文 明确930金融网络营销新规具体要求】监管正强调与督促券商、基金公司落地实施“930新规”。《金融产品网络营销管理办法》已于今年9月30日正式实施，记者多方获悉，近期已有多地证监局向辖区内机构提出具体工作要求，总体来看，一是不得与第三方互联网平台以外的任何组织或者个人（包括“网络大V”）合作开展网络营销；二是与平台合作须坚持业务独立、技术安全、数据保密，付费不得与开户量、交易量、手续费等指标挂钩；三是为证券交易提供转接渠道的平台须向证监会备案。此外，机构还须建立平台事前评估机制，加强自主运营App建设，不得与未完成备案的平台开展转接渠道合作，存量合作须在《办法》实施1年内整改完毕，并按季度报送合作情况。

title: Trump says he’s reached a deal with Putin to supply Russian diesel to U.S. and global markets. Zelensky calls it ‘an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.’
content_preview: U.S. President Donald Trump said he had reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply Russian diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets. Trump said they reached the agreement during “highly successful” talks by phone. Russia agreed to supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets as soon as possible, Trump said. It will supply another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons “immediately thereafter.” “Based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries,” Moscow could also supply another 3 million metric tons of diesel “within a short period of time,” Trump said. Trump’s announcement came as the U.S. Treasury Department issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel fuel to be supplied to the global market until April 7, 2027. “Thanks to our total control of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump said. title: The Kyiv Independent: Russia wants sanctions lifted in exchange for halting strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure
content_preview: Russian authorities have asked the United States to lift sanctions as part of talks on an “energy ceasefire,” The Kyiv Independent reported, citing Ukrainian and American sources. Russian officials are also trying to link sanctions relief to a ceasefire in the Black Sea, according to the outlet’s sources. Ukrainian officials familiar with the talks said they did not know exactly which sanctions Moscow wants lifted. A European diplomatic source said separately that the issue could involve returning control of frozen assets to Russia. If Russia gains access to the funds, he stressed, “the likelihood that these will be used to escalate [the war] is almost guaranteed.” “No one really thinks they are genuinely seeking to adhere to a ceasefire,” the outlet’s source stressed. Ukrainian authorities insist the energy ceasefire must be mutual and that Russia should receive no preferences in exchange for halting the strikes. Reports that Moscow is seeking sanctions relief in exchange for halting strikes on Ukraine’s energy system emerged as Russian attacks intensified. The Kyiv Independent said Russian authorities may be trying to secure a stronger negotiating position in the talks. U.S. President Donald Trump said September 14 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop striking each other’s energy infrastructure. Mutual strikes continued anyway. According to Axios, Trump’s special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to present the Ukrainian delegation with “new ideas and proposals” for ending the war during talks in the United States on October 9. By the end of the month, the outlet said, they plan to travel to Russia to discuss the “new ideas” with Russian leadership. The outlet did not specify what the proposals entail. title: Russia proposes raising maximum age for women’s military service
content_preview: The Russian government has submitted a bill to the State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, that would raise the maximum age for women in military service from 45 to 50. The bill appears in the State Duma’s database. The bill would also raise the maximum age for women to remain in the reserves: to 55 for officers, up from 50, and to 50 for those with other ranks, up from 45. The explanatory note says the bill is necessary to create “additional social guarantees for female service members.” Its authors say the current maximum age for military service does not always allow women to serve long enough to qualify for a pension and other benefits. For example, a woman who signs a contract between ages 25 and 30 and serves in a location “where preferential pension service credit does not apply” may not receive subsidized housing or a pension after reaching the maximum age for military service. The government also stressed that, amid the war with Ukraine, most of the personnel in medical units are women service members, “including those who have reached (or are reaching) the maximum age for military service.” In July 2023, Vladimir Putin signed a law that raised the maximum age for remaining in the reserves by five years for certain citizens holding military ranks. The amendments set new age limits for soldiers, sailors, sergeants, petty officers, warrant officers, and midshipmen. title: Ukrainian drone alert disrupts Russian government flights returning from Putin’s Turkmenistan trip
content_preview: Several aircraft from Russia’s Rossiya Special Flight Detachment, which transports the country’s leaders and senior officials, circled over Moscow on the evening of October 9 because of the threat of a Ukrainian drone attack. Five of the detachment’s aircraft were unable to land immediately. At least three were returning from Turkmenistan, where Russian President Vladimir Putin had attended a Commonwealth of Independent States summit, several Russian news outlets and Telegram channels reported ( 1 , 2 , 3 ). All three were Il-96s, the type used to transport the president, Agentstvo reported . According to Flightradar24, two Il-96s with registration numbers RA-96020 and RA-96022 circled over Moscow and the surrounding region. They departed Turkmenbashi Airport at 2 p.m. and 2:15 p.m. and landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport at 6:06 p.m. and 6:21 p.m., respectively. A third Il-96, with registration number RA-96025 , departed Turkmenbashi at 3:52 p.m. and flew over Moscow even though it was scheduled to land at Vnukovo. It was eventually diverted to St. Petersburg’s Pulkovo Airport and later departed for Moscow. Restrictions were imposed at all Moscow airports around 3:40 p.m. and fully lifted by 6:40 p.m. According to estimates from Ostorozhno, Novosti, more than 200 flights were delayed and more than 100 canceled amid the restrictions. It is unclear which aircraft Putin was aboard. At 1:52 p.m., TASS reported that the president had ended his visit to Turkmenistan and boarded one of the Rossiya detachment’s aircraft, which was preparing to depart Turkmenbashi. title: Four families, four stories of separation. The authors of ‘Stolen Youth,’ a new book from Meduza about how Russia abducted thousands of Ukrainian children, explain why they wrote it.
content_preview: Since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022, thousands of Ukrainian children have ended up in Russia. The scenarios varied: some fled the combat zone, and the only way out led through the Russian border; others were taken from occupied territories deeper into the occupying country, often under false pretenses, such as a school trip; still others were sent by their own parents to Russian children’s camps to escape the danger, only for the parents to later find they couldn’t get them back. The Russian state made active use of this: it placed the children with new families and even issued them new passports on an expedited basis. In 2023, the International Criminal Court in The Hague ruled that the removal of children from Ukraine was a war crime. Journalists Nina Nazarova (Russia) and Sviatoslav Khomenko (Ukraine) have collected in their book ” Stolen Youth: How Russia Kidnaps Ukrainian Children — And How Ukrainians Get Them Back ” four different stories of families who fell victim to this crime, and have also described in detail those who organized the removal of children, and those who are still helping bring them home. We published this book together with the StraightForward Foundation , which helps create uncensored nonfiction about Russia. Nina Nazarova, coauthor of ‘Stolen Youth’ This book began in April 2022. I was watching a conference of Russian officials live on YouTube for work — usually a dreary spectacle. But this video stunned me: For the first time, I heard officials openly acknowledge that they had brought thousands of Ukrainian children into Russia, including from Ukrainian cities that the Russian army had just destroyed. At that moment, a year before the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova on suspicion of unlawfully deporting Ukrainian children, some journalistic instinct told me that these children would become a central issue in this war. title: ‘We’re being used as a front,’ Zelensky says of Trump’s diesel deal with Putin
content_preview: Russia and the U.S. have agreed on a deal to supply Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. and global markets. President Donald Trump announced the agreement on the evening of October 9 after a phone call with Vladimir Putin. Trump called the talks “highly successful.” Putin confirmed that Russia is ready to supply oil and petroleum products to the U.S. and global markets. The U.S. said it is easing sanctions on Russian diesel. The Treasury Department has already issued a temporary license allowing sales of Russian diesel on the global market through April 7, 2027, despite U.S. sanctions. Washington previously eased sanctions on Russian oil temporarily because of a market crisis caused by the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran. Russia has also begun lifting restrictions on diesel exports , Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said. Sanctions and domestic export bans restrict exports of Russian oil and petroleum products worldwide. A ban on diesel and marine fuel exports by producers, for example, remains in effect through the end of October. Russia imposed it amid Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and a domestic fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian attacks over the summer. Trump said the two sides agreed on the “immediate” delivery of more than 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel. Russia will supply another 500,000 metric tons in November, followed by an additional million metric tons. Novak said Russia is ready to supply additional diesel to the U.S. market as early as October. Exports are also expected to rise in November and December as refineries resume operations after repairs. Ukraine criticized the diesel deal between Moscow and Washington. President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media that any easing of sanctions on Russia without agreements on de-escalation shows “obvious weakness.” “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. title: First Russian to sue organizers of Kanye West’s canceled concerts receives 132,000-ruble ticket refund
content_preview: Say Agency, the organizer of Kanye West’s canceled concert in St. Petersburg, has refunded 132,000 rubles to Voronezh resident Yevgeny Rasskazov, the first person in Russia to sue the company over the cancellation, his representative told TASS. Rasskazov received the money on October 5. His representative said the refund covered the face value of four tickets. Rasskazov has yet to receive the additional 13,200 rubles he paid when buying them (likely a service fee). His representative said Rasskazov had revised his claims against the concert organizer. He is asking the court to order the company to pay him 50% of the ticket price, a penalty for the delayed refund, and 30,000 rubles in compensation for emotional distress. Rasskazov filed his lawsuit against Say Agency on September 9. In mid-August, Say Agency said Kanye West would perform at Gazprom Arena in St. Petersburg in October. The organizers said they had sold more than 100,000 tickets. Gazprom Arena representatives later said there was no agreement to rent the stadium for West’s concerts, meaning the event would not take place. On September 17, listings for the Russian concerts disappeared from the rapper’s website. Say Agency did not officially announce the cancellation of the performances until September 30. In early October, ticket buyers began receiving emails saying refunds would begin on October 12. According to Kommersant , St. Petersburg police have begun looking into possible fraud by Say Agency. They will send the materials they collect to the Interior Ministry’s headquarters in Moscow, where officials will decide whether there are grounds to open a criminal investigation. content_preview: On September 20, 2026, Ukraine launched another large-scale drone attack on the Moscow region. One drone hit a high-rise apartment building in Kotelniki, southeast of Moscow. Another had struck the same building in June. Neither strike killed anyone, but the attacks badly frightened many people in the neighborhood. Reporters from Bereg, a cooperative of independent journalists, visited the Novye Kotelniki residential complex to see how repairs were progressing after the two attacks and how residents had responded. title: More than a third of Russian companies forgo annual bonuses in 2026
content_preview: In total, 46.9% of Russian companies do not plan to pay employees end-of-year bonuses, with 36.2% forgoing bonuses only in 2026, despite having paid them a year earlier. The findings come from a survey of 1,076 companies across Russia conducted by Aktion Bukhgalteriya , Forbes Russia reported. Another 20.4% of respondents have postponed their bonus decisions indefinitely. Only 22.3% of those surveyed said they would pay bonuses to all employees. Another 10.4% said they would reward only part of their staff. A decline in this year’s financial results was the leading reason cited for skipping bonuses, named by 56.9% of survey respondents. Another 8.8% pointed to taxes and insurance contributions as the deciding factor. Experts attribute the trend to rising business costs. Russia’s corporate profit tax rose from 20% to 25% in 2025, and the value-added tax rose from 20% to 22% starting in 2026, alongside a lowered threshold for qualifying for the simplified tax system. At the same time, weak demand and a high key interest rate have made loans too expensive, while rising production costs are squeezing profitability and forcing companies to cut spending. Employees of small businesses will be hit hardest by these changes, according to Aktion Bukhgalteriya. Decisions at these companies more often hinge on a single person and current revenue. Large businesses, which have reserves and formalized bonus programs, will continue paying bonuses. However, some companies may replace annual bonuses with quarterly bonuses, paid training, or non-monetary incentives to avoid a buildup of financial obligations by December, experts say. title: ‘The smell of death is everywhere’: Inside the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where hundreds are trapped without food, electricity, or medicine
content_preview: A view of Oleshky Since 2022, residents of Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region have lived under occupation. In 2023, the city was flooded after the Kakhovka dam was blown up: the flooding destroyed dozens of residential blocks and all of its infrastructure. In the fall of 2026, Oleshky found itself cut off. There’s a humanitarian catastrophe there: the city has no electricity, food, or medicine. Every way out is mined and blocked by Russian troops. Meduza spoke to people who have miraculously managed to stay in touch with those who remain in Oleshky. Before the full-scale war, Nina used to bring her homemade milk every Thursday. “I had [about a third of an acre] of land, and I planted peony bushes all along the perimeter. The scent was intoxicating!” Svitlana says. “Nina asked why I didn’t take the flowers to market. But how could I sell something so beautiful?” Svitlana’s yard brimmed with flowers until autumn, and hers wasn’t the only one. “It was as if the townspeople were competing over whose front garden was more lavish. Oleshky bloomed and smelled wonderful.” Svitlana calls the land she lived on for three decades “rodiucha,” which translates from Ukrainian as “fertile”: Stick a branch in the ground and it will sprout. title: A Ukrainian missile strike killed 20 Russian officers in occupied Donetsk. It was the largest known loss of Russian officers in a single attack since the invasion, Mediazona reports.
content_preview: A Ukrainian missile strike on Donetsk on August 26 killed 20 Russian military officers, Mediazona reported. The outlet said this was the largest number of Russian army officers killed in a single incident since the war began. The officers served at the headquarters of the Central Military District and the 41st Combined Arms Army. Mediazona confirmed their deaths by cross-checking personnel rosters against probate records and reviewing obituaries of high-ranking officers published over the past month. Denis Pushilin, the head of the annexed Donetsk People’s Republic, said on August 26 that Ukrainian forces had struck the area around the Donetsk City shopping mall with Storm Shadow missiles. He said eight civilians had been wounded but gave no information about military casualties. An Izvestia correspondent at the scene reported in a post that 10 people had been killed, but the post was later deleted . title: Russian prosecutors cancel criminal case against investigator over missing jewelry seized from influencer Valeria Chekalina
content_preview: Update: Prosecutors have overturned the decision to open a criminal investigation into Nikita Tulupov, an investigator in the Lerchek case, TASS reported. Some of the jewelry seized during a search of blogger Valeria Chekalina’s home has gone missing, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Irina Volk said on Telegram. Authorities opened a criminal investigation into one of the investigators in the case against Chekalina, who is known as Lerchek. The jewelry “was not entered into evidence in the criminal case and was stored improperly, resulting in its loss,” Volk said. Volk said a criminal investigation had been opened into the investigator for allegedly exceeding his authority. She did not name him. Jewelry from Cartier, Graff, Van Cleef & Arpels, Rolex, Chopard, and other brands, worth a total of 14.4 million rubles, was seized during a search in the case against Chekalina and her former husband. “Once the investigation was over, we asked for all the jewelry seized during the search to be returned, but the investigator refused, even though the jewelry is not physical evidence and no legal restrictions had been placed on it,” Chekalina’s lawyer, Viktor Dugin, told TASS. Valeria Chekalina appeared on Forbes’ list of Russia’s highest-earning bloggers. In 2023, she and her husband, Artem Chekalin, were charged with tax evasion and money laundering. title: 中共中央政法委：甲醛白菜等冲击食安底线 要下猛药出重拳
content_preview: 中国接连发生多起食品安全事件，中央政法委高调部署食品安全违法犯罪查处工作，指“甲醛白菜”等事件严重冲击食品安全底线，要求督办一批重大案件，严惩一批违法犯罪分子，“下猛药、出重拳”，释放依法严惩的强烈信号。 据新华社星期一（10月12日）报道，中央政法委近期印发《关于依法从严查处危害食品安全违法犯罪的意见》（下称《意见》），要求政法机关依法从严查处危害食品安全违法犯罪。 中央政法委有关负责人表示，中国食品安全形势总体平稳可控，稳中向好，但同时也出现了一些新情况、新问题，相关领域食品安全犯罪仍高发频发，特别是近期发生的“甲醛白菜”“敌敌畏消杀”“药水杨梅”等事件严重冲击食品安全底线，引发社会广泛关注。 负责人表示，要坚持以人民为中心，聚焦社会高度关切的肉制品、校园食品、保健食品、蔬菜水果等重点领域，督办一批重大案件，严惩一批违法犯罪分子。 负责人还说，要坚持严的主基调，“始终保持严字当头、一严到底的高压态势，对那些利欲熏心、挑战道德和良知底线的不法分子，下猛药、出重拳，发现一起，查处一起。通过刑罚惩戒大幅提高违法犯罪成本，形成有力震慑，倒逼生产经营者守法自律”。 《意见》突出强调“依法从严查处”，包括突出打击重点，聚焦社会高度关切的肉制品、校园食品、保健食品、蔬菜水果等重点领域，生产加工、网络销售、终端餐饮、食品进口等重点环节，深挖案件线索，严惩违法犯罪分子，释放依法严惩的强烈信号。 意见也提出，对侦查、逮捕、起诉、审判、刑罚执行等刑事诉讼全过程、各环节依法从严提出要求，要求依法严格控制缓刑、免予刑事处罚适用，对情节严重、影响恶劣的依法从重判罚。 《意见》也要求，要切实解决案件标准不明确、移送程序不规范、以罚代刑、当罚不罚等问题、提高行刑衔接效率、健全行刑反向衔接机制，促进行政处罚与刑事处罚双向衔接、无缝对接。 中共中央政治局委员、中央政法委书记陈文清9月24日主持召开专题会议时对“甲醛白菜”等危害食品安全事件作出强烈回应，强调要依法从严查处违法犯罪，全链条惩处涉食安违法分子，守护群众“舌尖上的安全”。

title: Russia opens criminal fraud case against former co-owner of retail chains Lenta and Rive Gauche
content_preview: Dmitry Kostygin, the former co-owner of the Russian supermarket chain Lenta and the Rive Gauche chain, has been detained, the Russian business news outlet RBC and the St. Petersburg-based news outlet Fontanka reported, citing sources. On October 8, a Moscow court placed Kostygin under house arrest. According to Fontanka, Kostygin is accused of concealing Yulmart’s true financial position when he and accomplices signed a 2017 contract on Yulmart’s behalf with a company called Berks to supply equipment and machinery. Kostygin, a former co-owner of the retailer Yulmart, was named a suspect in a criminal fraud case in 2017. August Meyer, another co-owner of the chain, was also charged in the case. The businessmen were accused of misappropriating loans Yulmart had received from Sberbank and VTB for business development, with total damage estimated at 3.14 billion rubles. In 2024, a court sentenced Kostygin to four years in prison and Meyer to three years. Both were exempted from serving their sentences after the statute of limitations expired. title: 曾与覃伟中搭档 深圳市委原常委王守睿主动投案
content_preview: 中国经济特区深圳市原市长覃伟中落马数周后，曾与他搭档的中共深圳市委原常委王守睿官宣被查。官方称，被查前掌管“特区中的特区”深圳前海的王守睿，是主动向组织交代问题。 广东省纪委监委星期一（10月12日）公布，深圳市委原常委、前海深港现代服务业合作区党工委原书记王守睿涉嫌严重违纪违法，主动向组织交代问题，目前正接受广东省纪委监委纪律审查和监察调查。 官方简历显示，王守睿是山东菏泽人，60岁的他已达退休年龄，过往职业生涯横跨高校、企业与地方党政系统，从政后担任过深圳市罗湖区委副书记、政法委书记、常务副区长，深圳市政府口岸办公室党组书记、主任等职。 2021年7月，王守睿任深圳市宝安区委书记，2023年7月任深圳市副市长、宝安区委书记，后兼任前海深港现代服务业合作区党工委副书记，2024年5月任深圳市委常委，兼任前海合作区党工委书记、前海管理局局长。 王守睿今年9月上旬还以深圳市委常委、前海合作区党工委书记、前海管理局局长的身份多次公开露面。前海全称“前海深港现代服务业合作区”，被官方视为“特区中的特区”。中国官媒曾形容，推进前海开发开放，是中共总书记习近平“亲自谋划、亲自部署、亲自推动的国家改革开放重大举措”。 早前担任深圳市副市长期间，王守睿曾搭档深圳前任市长覃伟中。今年8月，覃伟中因“工作岗位变动”辞去深圳市长职务，随后改任广东省人大常委会党组成员，并在9月21日官宣被查。

title: 【习近平同巴布亚新几内亚总督达达埃就中巴新建交50周年互致贺电 李强同巴新总理马拉佩互致贺电】新华社北京10月12日电
content_preview: 【习近平同巴布亚新几内亚总督达达埃就中巴新建交50周年互致贺电 李强同巴新总理马拉佩互致贺电】新华社北京10月12日电 10月12日，国家主席习近平同巴布亚新几内亚独立国总督达达埃互致贺电，庆祝两国建交50周年。 习近平指出，巴新是中国在太平洋岛国地区的好朋友、好伙伴、好兄弟。两国建交半个世纪以来，政治互信不断深化，互利合作成果丰硕，人文交流日益拓展，双边关系长足发展，不仅造福了两国人民，也为构建中国同太平洋岛国命运共同体注入强劲动力。 习近平强调，我高度重视中国同巴新关系发展，愿同达达埃总督一道努力，以两国建交50周年为契机，赓续传统友好，加强各领域交流合作，引领中巴新全面战略伙伴关系再上新台阶，更好惠及两国人民。 达达埃表示，建交50年来，巴新同中国关系取得长足发展，惠及两国和两国人民。巴新珍视同中国的长期友谊，坚定恪守一个中国原则，期待以两国建交50周年为契机，推动双边关系持续深入发展。 同日，国务院总理李强同巴新总理马拉佩互致贺电。李强表示，中方愿同巴新方一道努力，以建交50周年为契机，加快推进高质量共建“一带一路”，推动中巴新全面战略伙伴关系不断向前发展。 马拉佩表示，巴新政府高度赞赏中国为巴新经济社会发展所作重大贡献。巴新方将继续恪守长期坚持的一个中国原则，同中方深化各领域互利合作，推动双方全面战略伙伴关系不断发展。（新华社）

title: How Low Can the Strategic Petroleum Reserve Actually Go?
content_preview: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve held just 283 million barrels of oil at the end of September, according to Reuters, the lowest level since October 1982, back when the reserve was still being filled for the first time. It's a scary-looking number, and most of the coverage has treated it that way. But the barrel count is the easy part of this story. Oil came out of those Gulf Coast salt caverns fast, because that's exactly what the system was built to do. Getting it back in is slower, more expensive and more dependent on things nobody controls.…

title: Pemex Needs Nearly $110 Billion to Hit Mexico's Output Targets

title: 【视频】广东岸外渔船起火遭严重烧毁 八船员全获救无伤亡
content_preview: 一艘渔船在中国广东汕尾马宫港附近海域突发起火，渔船遭烧毁，但所幸受困八名船员全被救出，无人伤亡。 据中国央视新闻报道，广东汕尾海警局上星期五（10月9日）晚间接到报警，马宫港附近海域一艘作业渔船突发起火，八名船员被困，情况十分危急。 报道称，当晚事发海域风浪较大，大风加剧了渔船火势蔓延，现场救援条件复杂，处置风险较高。 视频显示，渔船几乎遭大火吞噬，火光照亮夜空。明火被扑灭后，渔船遭烧毁的痕迹清晰可见。 为保障船员生命安全，海警执法员在赶赴现场途中，远程协调距离事发点最近的渔船先行开展救援，协助被困船员转移避险。 报道称，救援舰艇抵达现场时，八名被困船员已被过往渔船安全救出。执法员随即综合研判火情、海况和船舶状况，架设灭火装备开展扑火作业。 渔船明火被彻底扑灭，未出现人员伤亡情况。渔船起火原因还在进一步调查中。 （视频来源：CCTV+）

title: 美媒：特朗普政府6月以来在机场拘留至少12名合法留美港人
content_preview: 美国媒体报道，特朗普政府自6月以来，在机场拘留至少12名合法留美港人。 美国政治新闻网站POLITICO星期天（10月11日）引述被拘留港人及其代表律师报道，尽管前任总统拜登（Joe Biden）政府时期签署的指令，允许香港人在美国合法居住和工作至2027年2月，但美国移民及海关执法局（ICE）人员自6月以来，已在机场拘留至少12名香港人。 据报道，ICE官员威胁被拘留者，若不签署自愿离境文件将被无限期拘禁。一名香港人7月在芝加哥机场准备登机时被拘留，称“ICE人员强迫我签署一份自愿离境文件。他们说‘如果你不签，将在牢里呆上数个月’”。 主管ICE的美国国土安全部拒绝就个别案例予以置评，但在一份声明中表示，授予香港人的工作许可“并不赋予其在美国的合法身份”。 报道称，移民法庭已对上述12名香港人的案件予以裁决，12人均从ICE拘留中获释，但仍需配戴电子脚镣，且出行范围受限。 ICE对他们的拘留时间从10天到两个月不等。 这些被拘留者的代表律师称，他们担心美国国土安全部上述操作是为日后将这些拘留者递解出境铺路，只要他们合法留美期限在明年2月届满，就可将他们遣返。 旧金山非营利组织亚裔法律联盟的移民正义项目主任维斯（Evelyn Wiese）表示，“ICE正在扩大对哪些人可以，以及应该被拘留的界定。这是更广泛趋势的一部分，即ICE故意拘留那些在法律上站不住脚的人，但由于许多人受到恐吓，无法及时聘请律师，ICE得以遣返更多人”。

title: 德国社民党联合主席巴斯宣布辞职
content_preview: 德国社会民主党联合主席、劳工部长巴贝尔·巴斯宣布辞去党主席职务，并请求德国总理解除其部长职务。在一封与社民党联合主席、德国副总理拉尔斯·克林拜尔共同发布的声明中，巴斯表示，目前她无力在短期内全面履行政府和党内职责，因此决定辞去上述职务。据悉，巴斯辞职之际，德国执政联盟中的联盟党与社民党近期均面临民意支持度下降的压力。 (央视新闻)

title: 北方稀土：预计2026年前三季度净利润36.2亿元到36.8亿元，同比增长134.95%到138.84%
content_preview: 北方稀土公告，预计2026年前三季度归属于母公司所有者的净利润36.2亿元到36.8亿元，同比增长134.95%到138.84%；扣除非经常性损益的净利润36.3亿元到36.9亿元，同比增长166.64%到171.04%。2025年前三季度归母净利润为15.41亿元，扣非净利润为13.62亿元。公司称，受稀土产品价格高位震荡、产品产量及销量增长、降本提质增效等因素影响，经营业绩同比大幅增长。

title: 汇丰将转向华尔街式薪酬结构 拟逐步淡化固定薪资并提高奖金占比
content_preview: 汇丰将逐步取消高级员工的固定薪酬津贴，转而将更大比例的薪酬改以奖金形式发放。一份备忘录显示，这家总部位于伦敦的银行正在转向更像华尔街式的薪酬结构，将于明年初开始逐步结束旧的固定薪酬制度。此举旨在更好地将薪酬与绩效挂钩，这是行政总裁艾桥智对该银行进行持续改革的又一举动。（彭博）

title: 吴清将参加2026金融街论坛年会并发表主题演讲
content_preview: 10月12日，在2026金融街论坛年会新闻发布会上，证监会办公厅副主任王利表示， 证监会主席吴清将出席10月19日论坛年会开幕式并作主题演讲，此外，多位证监会领导和有关司局、系统单位负责人也将出席论坛年会有关活动 。 王利介绍，10月21日，证监会承办一场主论坛，主题聚焦“建设一流投资机构，服务资本市场高质量发展，共享投资中国新机遇”，主论坛设领导致辞、主题演讲环节，还安排有两场圆桌交流，内容分别为培育壮大耐心资本和双向开放下的中国资本市场长期投资机遇，我们将邀请境内外知名行业机构的专家，围绕产业赋能、投资趋势、合规发展、国际合作等开展交流。同时，证监会科技司将承办金融科技大会子论坛，主题为“AI赋能资本市场数智化”，聚焦AI+资本市场的实践与监管、AI驱动资本市场数字化变革新趋势等主题，探讨AI赋能背景下资本市场发展的新模式、新场景。北京证券交易所将承办一场平行论坛，主题为“共建服务中小企业资本市场新生态”，围绕提升资本市场韧性与活力、全球资本市场服务科技创新实践、北交所赋能中小企业创新发展等开展研讨交流，并发布相关战略合作成果。（证券时报）

title: 教育部：超12万个专业点 我国职业教育基本涵盖国民经济各领域
content_preview: 从教育部今天召开的新闻发布会获悉，我国建成了世界上规模最大且有质量的现代职业教育体系，在层次体系上，完成了“中等职业教育—高职专科教育—职业本科教育”的布局，截至2025年底，全国有中等职业学校（含技工学校）9151所，高职专科学校1554所。 目前，职业本科学校共有124所，另有52所普通高校开设职业本科专业，打破了职业教育层次仅限于专科的“天花板”。在专业体系上，截至2025年底，职业教育设置19个专业大类、97个专业类、1491个专业，全国职校专业点超12万个，覆盖全部41个工业大类，基本涵盖国民经济各领域。（央视新闻）

title: Райнхард Май в 83 года установил рекорд немецкого чарта
content_preview: Новый альбом Райнхарда Мая "Schatzhauser" обошел по популярности записи многих мировых звезд. Музыкант стал самым пожилым исполнителем, которому удалось возглавить официальный альбомный чарт.
